title: Plato, Aristotle and Greek sayings
note: Classical Attic, the Greek of Plato and Aristotle, is the parent of Koine and reads much the same. Watch for Attic ττ where Koine has σσ (θάλαττα, θάλασσα) and for crasis, two words merged into one (κἀγαθός = καὶ ἀγαθός). Some famous sayings are traditional rather than exact quotations; the notes in parentheses say who said or is credited with each.

items.c: ὁ δὲ ἀνεξέταστος βίος οὐ βιωτὸς ἀνθρώπῳ
items.a: The unexamined life is not worth living for a human being. (Socrates)
d: The examined life is too hard for a human being. (Socrates)
A human life is not worth examining. (Socrates)
items.r: ho de anexetastos bios ou biōtos anthrōpō

items.c: Πάντες ἄνθρωποι τοῦ εἰδέναι ὀρέγονται φύσει.
items.a: All human beings by nature desire to know. (Aristotle)
d: All human beings by nature desire to be happy. (Aristotle)
By nature few human beings want to know. (Aristotle)
items.r: Pantes anthrōpoi tou eidenai oregontai physei.

items.a: A human being is by nature a political animal. (Aristotle)
d: A human being is by nature a rational animal. (Aristotle)
A human being by nature loves the city. (Aristotle)

items.a: I know one thing: that I know nothing. (Socrates)
d: I know nothing about one thing. (Socrates)

items.a: The beginning is half of the whole. (proverb)
d: Half of everything is the end. (proverb)

items.a: noble and good: a true gentleman
The body is a tomb. (Platonic wordplay)
d: The body is a temple. (Platonic wordplay)
The body is the soul. (Platonic wordplay)

items.a: God always does geometry. (credited to Plato)
d: God never plays dice. (credited to Plato)
God always speaks in riddles. (credited to Plato)

items.a: Let no one ignorant of geometry enter. (the Academy)
d: Let no one without wisdom speak. (the Academy)
Let everyone here learn geometry. (the Academy)

items.c: Ὁ βίος βραχύς, ἡ δὲ τέχνη μακρή.
items.a: Life is short, and the art is long. (Hippocrates)
d: Life is long, and the art is short. (Hippocrates)
Life is an art, and art is life. (Hippocrates)
items.r: Ho bios brachys, hē de technē makrē.

items.a: A human being is the measure of all things. (Protagoras)
d: God is the measure of all things. (Protagoras)
Money is the measure of all things. (Protagoras)

read.title: Socrates and his students
text: Σωκράτης ἦν φιλόσοφος Ἀθηναῖος. ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἠρώτα τοὺς νεανίας· Τί ἐστιν ἀρετή; τί ἐστιν τὸ ἀγαθόν; οἱ δὲ νεανίαι οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον. Σωκράτης δὲ ἔλεγεν· Ἓν οἶδα, ὅτι οὐδὲν οἶδα.
Πλάτων, ὁ μαθητὴς αὐτοῦ, ἔγραψεν πολλοὺς λόγους περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς καὶ τῆς δικαιοσύνης. Ἀριστοτέλης δέ, ὁ μαθητὴς τοῦ Πλάτωνος, ἔγραψεν ὅτι πάντες ἄνθρωποι τοῦ εἰδέναι ὀρέγονται φύσει.

q.q: What did Socrates ask the young men?

o: that the soul is a tomb
that the unexamined life is not worth living
that all human beings by nature desire to know
